Now, before you think I'm trying to get in the competition with voat and reddit, let me tell you that I'm not a programmer and that the reason that got me thinking about this is completely different: I realized some time ago that the platform my college used felt really ineffective. I'm not sure if the problem is with the program or with the way my college uses it, but its probably the later. In my college, we have to use separate accounts for each department, and since its possible to get disciplines from multiple departments, you usually end up with 3 different accounts. Also, I realized people don't go there to discuss relevant things, they prefer to talk about those in facebook groups and the platform lacks a facebook integration. Lastly I think the design is pretty bad.

Anyways this kind of made me think... we have all these college professors who work in the field and actually USE the software to communicate with the students... so why don't they just go and improve it? Hell.. we have a bunch of students full of ideas and energy and yet none of them seems to have taken a step towards making it much better. There have been some improvements over the years, don't take me wrong, but still it seems very outdated and, like I pointed out, very diffuse. Because yes, today people want practicity. They want everything to be at the same place, like with mobiles. So having to log into a platform just to see my assignment for the day and then log back in to send it doesn't seem to fit our modern thinking. Not having a place to discuss scientific stuff... not having access to students from other areas... Like.. what if I want to start a project with people from the health department and maybe I wanna go into their hub and show my ideas and ask who approves... Why can't we have a voat-like discussion system and maybe some duolingo like exercises made by the professors... is it too hard or are people just not interested in doing that?

Tl;dr: Why don't students and professors work together to improve the platform of universities, to integrate them with other social media and make academic discussion much more organized and centered in a single spot instead of so diffuse? Is it so hard to program and design this kind of stuff? How hard would it take for an amateur to learn that, if it's even possible?
How hard is it to build a discussion platform like Voat? What about an interactive one like Khan Academy or Duolingo?

It's not so much hard to build as it is hard to make scale to millions of users. In fact, reddit's source code is freely available for anyone to use, so if you know what you're doing, you can just reuse it.

The harder part about getting something deployed like that in an institution is the bureaucracy surrounding it. The project would be approved by a department for investigation, then IT would chime in about how they'd want (for bullshit reasons) to reuse their existing infrastructure to integrate into it, and what about handling alumni vs students vs professors? Then of course legal would need to sign off on it, and given the climate of a lot of higher ed, there would also be a review of how every single interest group would be well-served.

By the time you make enough changes to any platform to satisfy everyone who has to approve a project, the project is ruined for everyone.

Far better to just make it unofficial, host it on the cheap somewhere (or just use voat itself), and tell your friends.
